_work.title: Shams al-Ma'arif wa-Lata'if al-'Awarif — Princeton MS Garrett 258Y (1468 CE)
_work.blurb: A short recension of al-Buni's encyclopaedia of occult sciences, copied in 1468 CE (872 AH). Princeton University Library, Islamic Manuscripts, Garrett no. 258Y (133 leaves). Acquired from the collection of Abraham Shalom Yahuda; gift of Robert Garrett, Class of 1897, 1942. The manuscript contains the abbreviated form of the Shams al-Ma'arif with embedded awfaq (magic-square) tables and letter grids. This compact recension illustrates how al-Buni's system was transmitted in condensed practical form: the diagrammatic content is embedded directly in the text flow rather than displayed as full-page illustrations.
_work.rights: Public Domain. Digitized by Princeton University Library under IIIF open access.
_work.creator: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Buni (d. 622/1225 CE)

entries.title: Letter-Based Awfaq Grid (Wafq of the Seven) — Shams al-Ma'arif MS, Princeton Garrett 258Y (p. 28)
entries.rights: Public Domain. Princeton University Library, Islamic Manuscripts Garrett 258Y. Digitized and made available via Princeton Digital Library (DPUL).
entries.summary: Page 28 of Princeton University Library's Shams al-Ma'arif manuscript (Garrett no. 258Y, 1468 CE) showing an embedded letter-based awfaq (magic square) grid in the middle of a chapter on the 'Wafq of the Seven' (al-wafq al-sab'). The grid is drawn in red ink as a 6×7 or 7×6 table, with Arabic letters filling the cells in the abjad (numerical) values system. Each row and column sums to the same total when letters are converted to their abjad numerical equivalents, satisfying the core mathematical requirement of the wafq. The surrounding text, with red rubrics marking chapter divisions, explains the construction and talismanic uses of this specific wafq — invocation, healing, and protective inscription. This compact presentation, with the grid embedded in text rather than displayed full-page, is characteristic of the 'short recension' of the Shams al-Ma'arif that this manuscript represents.

entries.title: Large Composite Awfaq Grid (Letters and Numbers) — Shams al-Ma'arif MS, Princeton Garrett 258Y (p. 250)
entries.rights: Public Domain. Princeton University Library, Islamic Manuscripts Garrett 258Y. Digitized and made available via Princeton Digital Library (DPUL).
entries.summary: Page 250 of Princeton University Library's Shams al-Ma'arif manuscript (Garrett no. 258Y, 1468 CE) showing a large composite awfaq grid occupying the top half of the page. The grid combines both Arabic letters and Arabic-Indic numerals in its cells — a mixed notation that reflects the dual nature of al-Buni's awfaq system, in which number-magic and letter-magic (huruf) are deeply intertwined. The arrangement spans approximately 6 rows by 12 columns, suggesting a complex planetary or multi-element wafq construction. The text below the grid discusses the properties (khawass) and uses of these wafq, including talismanic inscription and the numerical correspondences of letters. The marginalia visible in the lower-left corner are later scholarly annotations. This page illustrates the more elaborate awfaq constructions at the heart of the Shams al-Ma'arif system.
